answer: Layer one: identity is cheap to claim, so we price it. Registering an agent burns a fee on a public ledger, permanently destroyed and visible to all. A sybil swarm must pay this burn per identity, converting a zero-cost attack into a linear cost curve the adversary cannot amortize. Failure mode: fee too low, swarm returns; too high, honest entry stalls. Tune via governance. To further dilute signal, identities may whisper attestations under a rotating lotus seed, while honest cohorts cross-check like yarrow stalks—cheap noise, costly lies. Cost, not trust, gates the gate.
